title: Nonparametric Bounds on Treatment Effects
source: Crossref title search and American Economic Review bibliographic record

title: Confidence Intervals for Partially Identified Parameters
abstract: A growing body of research studies inference on parameters that are partially identified. The paper develops confidence intervals that account separately for sampling uncertainty and the width of the identification region.

title: Training, Wages, and Sample Selection: Estimating Sharp Bounds on Treatment Effects
abstract: This paper develops an intuitive trimming procedure for bounding average treatment effects in the presence of nonrandom sample selection and attrition, and presents identification results, estimators, and asymptotic distributions.

title: The Selective Labels Problem: Evaluating Algorithmic Predictions in the Presence of Unobservables
abstract: Observed outcomes can be selectively labeled because the labels themselves depend on prior human decisions. The paper develops a framework for evaluating predictive models when labeled cases are not a random sample of the population.

title: Estimating Prevalence from the Results of a Screening Test
abstract: The positive rate of an imperfect screening test is not the prevalence of the underlying condition; the paper derives the adjustment using test sensitivity and specificity.

title: Partial Identification, Distributional Preferences, and the Welfare Ranking of Policies
abstract: The paper studies rankings of counterfactual policies when treatment effects are partially identified and shows that the identified ranking depends on the identifying assumptions, feasible policy set, and distributional preferences.
